Chief_Complaint.content: 2–3 days of wheeze and shortness of breath

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Not woken at night by symptoms
No shortness of breath at rest
Occasional difficulty finishing sentences due to symptoms

Past_Medical_History.content: Asthma since childhood continuing into adulthood with hospital visits but no ICU admissions
Past_Medical_History.source_text: childhood → adult asthma (hospital visits, no ICU)

Medications.content: Salbutamol inhaler used as needed every few weeks, mainly pre-exercise
Medications.source_text: Meds: salbutamol inhaler PRN (q few wks, pre-exercise)

Medications.source_text: Increase salbutamol 2–4 puffs q4 h PRN

Medications.content: Start regular over-the-counter antihistamine for allergic rhinitis

Social_and_Family_History.content: Alcohol intake about 1 glass of wine every 2–3 days

Assessment.content: Asthma exacerbation, mild to moderate, likely viral or allergic trigger
Assessment.source_text: Asthma exacerbation (mild-mod); likely viral or allergic trigger

Plan_of_Care.content: Manage asthma exacerbation with increased salbutamol dosing
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Asthma exacerbation  • Increase salbutamol 2–4 puffs q4 h PRN

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe spacer and have pharmacist demonstrate its use
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Prescribe spacer; pharmacist to demonstrate use

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe peak-flow meter and record morning and evening values for 1 week
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Prescribe peak-flow meter; record AM & PM values x 1 wk

Plan_of_Care.content: Treat allergic rhinitis with regular over-the-counter antihistamine
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Allergic rhinitis  • Start regular OTC antihistamine

Plan_of_Care.content: Safety net advice to seek urgent care if worsening shortness of breath, inability to speak, or fever spikes
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Safety net: seek urgent care if worsening SOB, unable to speak, fever spikes
